- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment drops or stabilizes.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment or neutral sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — model tends to be overly conservative.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >78) — model often peaks too early and then corrects, so cap forecast at +5–10% above recent high if sentiment remains positive.
- Mean-reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day if sentiment is weak or flat.
- Lagged response: model often lags 1–2 days behind true price movements — adjust forecast by +0.5–1.5% for each day of lag if sentiment is trending.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate if sentiment is rising — reduce by 1–3% for each 0.10 increase in sentiment above 0.30.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price is flat, don’t assume continuation — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence.
